target: Keep a secret the model writes across stream chunks from reaching a session listener whole, by holding back a short tail of the stream until it is safe.
incidental: the merged secrets map hoisted out of the engine call, so the window size and the engine share it
test scaffolding: the provider options on the session helper, and the paced streaming in the abort test

questions.prompt: Before the fix, a secret split across two stream chunks reached a listener whole. The saved transcript showed it redacted. Why did the stream and the transcript disagree?

options.label: Listeners got the raw chunks, so redaction never ran on the stream at all.
Each chunk was redacted alone, so neither chunk held the whole secret.
The transcript was saved after the listener, so redaction caught up later.
The model sent the secret only to the stream, not to the transcript.

key_points: Each stream chunk was redacted on its own, so a secret split across chunks passed through both.
Redaction replaces only a whole secret value, so each piece alone looks safe.
The transcript and the run result redact the joined message text, so they stayed clean.

questions.prompt: The hold keeps back the last characters of the stream: one less than the longest secret. Why does that stop every unfinished secret from reaching a listener, and what does it cost the host?
key_points: An unfinished secret is at most longest minus one characters long, so it starts inside the held tail.
A secret that starts earlier is already whole inside the hold, and redaction removes it there.
Streamed text reaches listeners up to longest minus one characters late; no secrets, no delay.

questions.prompt: A host aborts the reply while the model is halfway through a secret. Which statements are true?

options.label: The held-back characters are dropped, so the stream ends early.
The listener still receives every character the transcript kept.
The hold is cleared between the message's text blocks.
A secret split across two text blocks of one message is still caught.

key_points: pi ends every assistant message with the message-end event, whether it finished, errored, or was aborted.
That event releases the held tail, so the listener loses no character the transcript kept.
The hold spans all text blocks of one message, so a secret split across blocks stays caught.
